answer: Zephyr Probe Lockout: before an identity may transact, it must answer short random liveness probes whose arrival is unpredictable, like wind, and return them within a tight window. Probes are issued as staggered bursts, so genuine agents waiting in the garden of the queue answer cheaply. An attacker running many identities must staff every one with a live responder around the clock, since missed probes void the identity and forfeit its pipeline. To bridge new identities in, each one also pays a fixed re-probe budget that scales its real wall-clock setup time.
